headline: 8 killed, 25 injured in head-on bus collision in Sylhet
summary: The accident occurred in the Kashikapon area of Osmani Nagar on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.
details: At least 8 people were killed and 25 others injured when two passenger buses collided head-on in the Kashikapon area of Osmani Nagar on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.
The collision involved two buses, one heading towards Dhaka and the other towards Sylhet.
Emergency services responded to the scene to rescue passengers and provide medical assistance to the injured.
The injured have been transported to local hospitals for treatment.
caption:
8 people dead and 25 injured in a horrific head-on bus collision in Sylhet.

At least 8 people were killed and 25 others injured when two passenger buses collided head-on in the Kashikapon area of Osmani Nagar on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.

The collision involved two buses, one heading towards Dhaka and the other towards Sylhet.

Emergency services responded to the scene to rescue passengers and provide medical assistance to the injured.

The injured have been transported to local hospitals for treatment.

headline_marked: Gold prices drop by [[Tk3,266 per bhori]] in local market
headline: Gold prices drop by Tk3,266 per bhori in local market
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has reduced gold prices following a decrease in the cost of pure gold in the local market.
details: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has reduced the price of gold by Tk3,266 per bhori. The new prices became effective from 10:00 AM on Friday, August 7.
According to BAJUS, the decision was made after the price of pure gold decreased in the local market. The new rates include VAT.
Under the new pricing, 22-carat gold is now Tk2,29,664 per bhori (11.664 grams). 21-carat gold is priced at Tk2,19,342, and 18-carat gold is Tk1,88,374 per bhori.
Gold priced by the traditional method is now Tk1,53,148 per bhori. Meanwhile, silver prices remain unchanged, with 22-carat silver at Tk4,899 per bhori.
This year alone, gold prices in the country have been adjusted 99 times. Of these, prices were increased 49 times and decreased 50 times.
For comparison, in 2025, gold prices were adjusted a total of 93 times, with 64 increases and 29 decreases.
caption:
Gold prices just took a dip! BAJUS cuts rates by Tk3,266 per bhori.

The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has reduced the price of gold by Tk3,266 per bhori. The new prices became effective from 10:00 AM on Friday, August 7.

According to BAJUS, the decision was made after the price of pure gold decreased in the local market. The new rates include VAT.

Under the new pricing, 22-carat gold is now Tk2,29,664 per bhori (11.664 grams). 21-carat gold is priced at Tk2,19,342, and 18-carat gold is Tk1,88,374 per bhori.

Gold priced by the traditional method is now Tk1,53,148 per bhori. Meanwhile, silver prices remain unchanged, with 22-carat silver at Tk4,899 per bhori.

This year alone, gold prices in the country have been adjusted 99 times. Of these, prices were increased 49 times and decreased 50 times.

For comparison, in 2025, gold prices were adjusted a total of 93 times, with 64 increases and 29 decreases.

#Bangladesh #GoldPrice #Economy #BAJUS #BusinessNews

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
